newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran guards attack in largest Gulf wargames.
newsitem.headline: Iran guards attack in largest Gulf wargames.

text.p: Ground, naval and air units of Iran's Revolutionary Guards attacked an imaginary enemy on Thursday in mock battles in Iran's largest Gulf wargames.

Iranian television, broadcasting live from a coastal area near the port of Bandar Abbas at the mouth of the Gulf, showed missile launches followed by an assault by artillery and armoured units with tanks and ground troops.

Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who has been in the strategic port since the start of the games on Tuesday, witnessed the operations with the guards' commander, Major-General Mohsen Rezaei, under overcast skies.
Rezaei said the assault was successful. Further exercises would be held in Bushehr in the northern Gulf and Kermanshah province bordering Iraq on Friday.
The amphibious wargames, codenamed "Tariq ol-Qods" (Road to Jerusalem), involve 200,000 members of the guards -- defenders of Iran's Islamic revolution -- and Basij militia volunteers.
Planned since last year, they are aimed at testing the ability to counter simultaneous threats in Iran's west and south.
They cover four provinces stretching from the mouth of the Gulf to the border with Iraq, Iran's enemy in an eight-year war which ended in 1988.

Khamenei, who is also commander-in-chief of Iran's armed forces, and other Iranian leaders have sought to reassure the Islamic republic's Gulf Arab neighbours about the defensive nature of the wargames.

They convey a message of peace and friendship to Gulf Arab states while displaying the might of Islam, one senior Iranian commander said. Guards commander Rezaei said on Monday Iran was ready to conclude a security pact with other Gulf states.

The oil-rich monarchies on the Arab side of the Gulf are suspicious of Iran and alarmed by an Iranian military buildup despite Tehran's assurances it is defensive. They have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, a charge denied by Tehran.

The six oil states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Oman -- have remained silent on the wargames and the offer of defence cooperation with their much larger Gulf neighbour.

Khamenei said on Wednesday that viewing the wargames as a threat to regional countries was U.S.-Israeli propaganda. They were not a threat to anyone whose intentions were not hostile, Iran's official news agency IRNA reported him as saying.
